outcome: Prevalence of hyperglycaemia first detected during pregnancy
Neonatal and maternal status at discharge
cohort: Pregnant women attending antenatal care (ANC) at St. Francis Hospital Nsambya, with no history of diabetes mellitus, at or after 24 weeks gestation
finding: The prevalence of hyperglycaemia first detected in pregnancy was high (31.9%) and was significantly associated with macrosomia.
